verdict.rationale: ByteAsk's own docs describe the whole debug loop. It builds and runs programs under AddressSanitizer to reproduce faults, attaches to a live gdb session through a bridge to read program state, and returns raw reports with frames, files and line numbers for root-cause analysis. It then reruns tests and the debugger so the diff it hands back has been verified. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the workflow works as claimed, and in-depth documentation of how root-cause narrowing proceeds beyond the sanitizer and gdb report.

support.subject: As a developer, I can reproduce issues, narrow down root causes, and verify fixes

citations.quote: then drives the real toolchain - sanitizers, your test suite, and any gdb session you already have open - and hands you a diff that survived the debugger.
ByteAsk joins through a bridge you start in your gdb, reads the live state, and asks before it changes anything.
It hands back the raw report with the frames, files and line numbers intact, so you can check the agent's reasoning against the same evidence.
A read-only run can still build your program under AddressSanitizer and run it.
edits files, compiles, runs tests, and presents a diff for your review before making permanent changes
